tagline: A roller coaster under the trees, pointed at Fayetteville.
intro: Just north of I-40 at Ozark, Highway 23 goes into the Ozark National Forest and starts to climb and fall. ARDOT likens the 19 miles to Brashears to a roller coaster, all steep grades and sharp curves, with the trees crowding in so close that in summer the road runs in shade in places.

Very little has been built along it, and Pig Trail Falls is there for anyone wanting to cool down. The traffic has its own tradition. This is the Razorback road, the way fans from central Arkansas come up to Fayetteville.

moments.title: Mulberry River
moments.text: A Wild and Scenic River with class I and II rapids, carried on the maps as Mulberry Creek until the Board on Geographic Names settled it in 1976.

moments.title: Brashears
moments.text: The trail runs out at Brashears Junction on Highway 16, just south of the upper White River, and the Razorback faithful carry on toward Fayetteville.

sources.label: Arkansas Tourism, Road Trip: The Scenic Byway Guide to Northwest Arkansas
